episode_title: LinkedIn on the Geography of Opportunity

real_qa.q: What does LinkedIn's Cities on the Rise study reveal about which cities are growing fastest in hiring and talent inflow?
real_qa.r: The Cities on the Rise study examined year-over-year growth in hiring and job postings on LinkedIn's platform, as well as inflows versus outflows of LinkedIn members to identify cities gaining larger percentages of people than they were losing. The analysis revealed standout cities not typically heard about, including Augusta, Georgia and Reno, Nevada, which showed growth in cybersecurity jobs and data center jobs.
real_qa.requete: Cities on the Rise LinkedIn study cities growing

real_qa.q: How much more likely are professionals to get hired when they know someone at the company they are applying to?
real_qa.r: Professionals who apply to jobs where they know somebody in their professional network are seven times more likely to actually get that job. This demonstrates a clear link between the network someone has and their career outcomes.

real_qa.q: What specific AI-related skills are employers looking for according to LinkedIn's Economic Graph data?
real_qa.r: LinkedIn is seeing two things come up really clearly: AI engineering and AI literacy skills are both really important. There is a huge premium around AI engineering skills like machine learning or agent development, as well as AI literacy skills like being able to use generative AI tools more broadly. Importantly, these skills must be combined with content expertise and human skills like collaboration, teamwork, creativity, and quality assessment.
real_qa.requete: AI skills employers demanding LinkedIn data

real_qa.q: Is entry-level hiring being impacted as severely as headlines suggest due to AI automation?
real_qa.r: Entry-level hiring is down, but it is actually not down as much as senior-level or managerial hiring year over year. What is more likely to be the case than AI taking all the jobs right now is that we are in an economic rough spot with different contributors to that. Right now, we are not seeing the entry-level job apocalypse that people talk about.
real_qa.requete: entry-level jobs AI impact hiring data

real_qa.q: What program does LinkedIn offer to help governments access economic data for development strategies at no cost?
real_qa.r: LinkedIn runs a program called Data for Impact, which leverages all of the data and insights that LinkedIn is sitting on and shares them in a privacy-preserving way to help local leaders determine how their economy is shifting based on LinkedIn data and make choices about their talent attraction strategy based on that.
real_qa.requete: Data for Impact LinkedIn program free

real_qa.q: Why does Casey Weston advise communities to build strategies based on existing local assets rather than chasing global tech hubs?
real_qa.r: Weston was speaking to leaders of Medellin who asked what they should do to become the next Silicon Valley. He dissuaded them from that approach not because they cannot, but because they have such a rich base of talent off which to develop a more meaningful strategy. Communities should start with what they have and think about how inputs like clean energy or AI can expand and amplify the existing strategy rather than trying to start from scratch.
real_qa.requete: economic development strategy local assets Medellin

guest.titre: Senior Manager of Public Policy and Economic Graph
guest.bio_context: Casey Weston is from St. Louis, Missouri, one of the most racially and economically segregated places in the country. His experience growing up observing these disparities led him to study urban policy and public policy to understand how places become segregated and how they can drive economic development forward in an equitable way. He currently leads research at LinkedIn's Economic Graph team, bridging economic data with public policy to help communities and individuals understand career outcomes and talent mobility.
